chunks: And al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me, from Abi al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abi Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Hafs ibn Abi 'Isa, who said:

I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: I stepped on excrement with my khuff, and I wiped it until I could no longer see anything on it. What do you say about performing salat (prayer) in it? He said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer); the act whose validity is being asked about
key_terms.بِخُفِّي: with my khuff; leather footwear or slipper referred to in the question
key_terms.عَذِرَةً: excrement; the impurity stepped upon in this ruling
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of permissibility in the ruling
key_terms.وَمَسَحْتُهُ: and I wiped it; removing the impurity by wiping

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in footwear after stepping on excrement and wiping it clean?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding najasah on footwear used in salat (prayer). It indicates that if excrement on a khuff is wiped away until no trace remains visible, then performing salat (prayer) in it is permitted.
